title: Rashmika Mandanna Is About to Play M.S. Subbulakshmi. It Might Be the Bravest Casting in Years.
excerpt: She's got four blockbusters releasing this year and Bollywood at her feet. But the role that could define Rashmika's legacy is a Carnatic music legend who moved millions without ever raising her voice.
body:
The most commercially dominant actress in Indian cinema just signed up to play the most spiritually revered singer in Indian history. And somehow, it makes perfect sense.

Rashmika Mandanna — fresh off her 30th birthday celebrations in April, with four confirmed theatrical releases stacked across 2026 — has reportedly been finalised to portray M.S. Subbulakshmi in an upcoming biopic directed by Gowtam Tinnanuri, the filmmaker behind Jersey. According to multiple industry sources, Rashmika has already undergone a secret look test at her Hyderabad residence, dressed in the legendary singer's signature traditional attire, with acclaimed costume designer Neeraja Kona crafting custom outfits for the session.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Qtsx4iDzMB4

If this casting holds, it won't just be Rashmika's first biopic. It will be the most audacious role of her career.

The Weight of the Name

For anyone who needs a reminder of who M.S. Subbulakshmi was — and if you do, this film is already for you — she was the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour. She was the first Indian musician to perform at the United Nations General Assembly. Her rendition of the Bhaja Govindam and Vishnu Sahasranamam is not just music in millions of Indian homes — it is the texture of mornings, the sound of prayer, the voice of devotion itself.

"Rashmika's expressions and certain facial features make her a strong contender for the role. She is said to be excited about the opportunity." — Source close to the production

Portraying someone of that stature requires more than talent. It requires surrender. And that's exactly what makes this casting so fascinating.

From Pushpa to Prayer

Rashmika Mandanna is, by any commercial metric, unstoppable. Her 2026 slate reads like a one-woman industry: Cocktail 2 with Shahid Kapoor and Kriti Sanon drops on June 19, the period historical Ranabaali alongside husband Vijay Deverakonda arrives in September, and the Allu Arjun science-fiction spectacle AA22xA6 closes the year in November. She is simultaneously Bollywood's most wanted romantic lead and Telugu cinema's biggest female draw.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZhsGzwMCqi/

But a biopic of M.S. Subbulakshmi is an entirely different register. This isn't about star power or screen presence — it's about stillness, about carrying the enormous emotional weight of a woman who moved millions without ever raising her voice above a melody. Reports suggest that Sai Pallavi and Rukmini Vasanth were previously considered for the role, both actresses known for their understated, naturalistic performances. That Rashmika ultimately won the part suggests the filmmakers saw something in her that the industry hasn't fully explored yet.

The Team Behind It

Gowtam Tinnanuri is no stranger to emotionally rich cinema. His Jersey, starring Nani, was a devastating portrait of ambition and fatherhood that went on to inspire a Bollywood remake. For the Subbulakshmi biopic, he's reportedly reuniting with composer Anirudh Ravichander — the man behind Jailer, Leo, and some of the most electrifying film scores in recent Tamil cinema. Anirudh scoring a film about Carnatic music's greatest voice is the kind of creative collision that could produce something genuinely transcendent.

Pre-production is reportedly in full swing, with an official announcement expected in the coming weeks.

Why the Diaspora Should Care

M.S. Subbulakshmi's music is the sound of the Indian diaspora's childhood. Her recordings travel in suitcases across oceans. They play in temples in New Jersey, in kitchens in London, in apartments in Toronto where grandmothers refuse to let go of the morning ritual. A film that does justice to her life wouldn't just be a biopic — it would be a homecoming.

And if Rashmika Mandanna can pull this off — if she can set aside the commercial superstardom, the brand endorsements, the blockbuster machinery, and disappear into a woman who was the opposite of all that noise — it won't just be a career-defining performance. It will be a cultural event.

The official announcement is coming. The look test is done. The music is being composed. Rashmika Mandanna is about to become M.S. Subbulakshmi. And Indian cinema might never be the same.
